#### Description
Found  during running community test **dualtor_io/test_link_failure.py::test_active_link_admin_down_config_reload_downstream[active-active]**

<!--
     Briefly describe the problem you are having in a few paragraphs.
-->

#### Steps to reproduce the issue:
1. Config Active-Active Dual-ToR setup, make sure that both switches have all mux ports active.
2. Shutdown ALL mux interface:

3. run traffic from T1 to the server via standby tor - traffic will go via tunnel 
4. `config save -y`
5. `config reload -y `
6. run traffic from T1 to the server via standby tor ---->  routes are not created, traffic will be dropped

comments.body:
I can confirm that we had a similar issue for Active-Standby on 202205, and it is fixed now.
But for Active-Active, it still reproduces on 202205 (which is really interesting)

comments.author: lolyu
comments.body:
Thanks @ayurkiv-nvda, I could reproduce this on `202205` branch, both on `active-active` and `active-standby`.

If all ports under a Vlan is admin `down`, the vlan device is not  in `running` state, so the route to the vlan subnet is flushed in ASIC. Thus any downstream traffic could not be trapped to the kernel, and as a result, no more tunnel route will be created.

comments.author: ayurkiv-nvda
comments.body:
Hello @lolyu 
Do we have some ETA for when this bug will be fixed?

comments.author: lolyu
comments.body: When all the member port is down, the vlan route is removed from the ASIC, the downstream traffic could not be trapped to the kernel. So the kernel will never try to learn the neighbor -> no FAILED neighbor -> no tunnel route. Will discuss further with the team if this could be further improved.

linkedPullRequests.title: [dualtor] Disable zebra link-detect for vlan interfaces
linkedPullRequests.author: lolyu
linkedPullRequests.body:
<!--
     Please make sure you've read and understood our contributing guidelines:
     https://github.com/Azure/SONiC/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md

     ** Make sure all your commits include a signature generated with `git commit -s` **

     If this is a bug fix, make sure your description includes "fixes #xxxx", or
     "closes #xxxx" or "resolves #xxxx"

     Please provide the following information:
-->

#### Why I did it
If all vlan member ports are admin down, the vlan route is removed by FRR, so the packets to the vlan subnet will be forwarded with the default route, two issues:
1. route inconsistency between kernel and ASIC.
the vlan route in kernel still has nexthop as the vlan device, the vlan route in ASIC has nexthop as the default route.
2. no tunnel will be created.
As those traffic will be bounced back to T1s by the ASIC, they will not be able to be trapped to kernel to trigger the zero-mac tunnel route creation.

For dualtor, the downstream standby traffic should be tunneled to the active side.
To ensure the zero-mac tunnel route works as expected, the vlan route should always present in both the kernel and ASIC.
So let's disable the link-detect for vlan interfaces.

Fixes: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/16085


Signed-off-by: Longxiang Lyu <lolv@microsoft.com>

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**: 26325737

#### How I did it
Disable the `link-detect` flag in the frr zebra template.

#### How to verify it
UT and nightly run.
